caption: The drawing depicts a detailed technical illustration of a side chair, shown from three perspectives: top view, front view, and side view. The drawing is executed on a cream-colored background with fine black ink lines that define the chair’s structure, and additional red lines and shading used for accents and measurements. The chair, made of mahogany, features an ornate back with interlacing, curved motifs and scroll details, a seat with rounded front corners, and cabriole legs with carved embellishments. The front two legs display elaborate scroll and floral carvings, while the side view shows the gentle backward curve of the chair’s backrest and the slight incline of the seat. Key measurements are written in red, including the overall height (42"), width of the seat (24¼"), and depth (21"), with additional measurements for seat width at the front (17¾") and at the back (22½"). Decorative labeling, done in black and red ink, identifies the drawing as a scale drawing of a Philadelphia mahogany side chair from the third quarter of the 18th century, with associated accession and location details from the Metropolitan Museum of Art, alongside the artist’s signature in the bottom right.
title: Side Chair
